title: Morning on the Lagos Bridge
body:
The sun climbs slow above the mainland haze,
the buses cough and shoulder into day.
A girl sells oranges beside the rail,
her laughter louder than the engines' bray.

I count the boats below like small white prayers
and think of you, still sleeping, far away.
A poem is a door you leave open for a stranger.

title: What Grief Taught Me
body:
Grief does not knock.
It lets itself in, sits in your chair,
drinks from your cup, learns your name,
and one day, without warning,
leaves the door ajar
so the light can find you.
We are all just verses looking for the song.

title: Night Shift
body:
Three a.m. and the city hums in minor key,
streetlights bowing to an empty road.
I write your name in condensation on the glass
and watch the letters run before I can decide
what I would have said.

title: Small Joys
body:
Warm bread. A letter.
Rain that ends before the walk home.
Your hand, finding mine without looking.
Love is the only language that forgives its own grammar.

title: Harmattan
body:
The dust arrives like an old relative,
uninvited, settling in every room.
Lips crack, the sky turns to milk,
and still the hibiscus insists on red.
